editorial:
If you have ever wanted a monster movie that feels like a mix of Godzilla and a fairy tale, Troll delivers exactly that. The story kicks off when an explosion in the Norwegian mountains wakes up a giant ancient troll, and the government calls in Nora, a fearless paleontologist, to figure out how to stop it. The movie has a fun, adventurous vibe with gorgeous mountain scenery and a creature that actually feels rooted in old Norwegian folklore. It never takes itself too seriously, which makes it easy to sit back and enjoy.

The action scenes are big and exciting, and the troll itself looks fantastic on screen. The pacing moves quickly, though some of the side characters feel a bit thin and the story follows a pretty familiar monster-movie formula. Still, the heart of the film comes from Nora and her bond with her father, who always believed trolls were real. If you love creature features and want something fun for movie night, this is a great pick.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Nora and her team lure the giant troll into direct sunlight, which turns it to stone and kills it. The twist comes right after, when a small baby troll is discovered hiding in the mountains, proving the species is not extinct. The government tries to cover everything up, but Nora and her allies know the truth. The movie ends on a hopeful note, hinting that more trolls could still be out there.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves monster movies and fantasy adventures.
